title: National Consumer Credit Protection Amendment (Small Amount Credit Contract and Consumer Lease Reforms) Bill 2019
short_title: National Consumer Credit Protection Amendment (Small Amount Credit Contract and Consumer Lease Reforms) Bill 2019

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would change payday lending and consumer lease rules by capping lease costs, regulating repayments and expanding obligations and penalties for providers.
Lease payments would be capped at the goods’ base price plus four per cent of that price per whole month, for up to 48 months.
The measures would start 12 months after royal assent, with specified delivery, installation and enforcement expenses excluded from the consumer lease payment cap.
changes: Payday loans would generally require equal instalments at equal intervals.
Lenders could not charge unused monthly fees after a payday loan is fully repaid early.
Household goods lease providers would need to obtain and consider 90 days of income bank statements.
Door-to-door sales of household goods leases would require a prior arrangement with a resident.
Regulations could set repayment limits linked to consumers’ income.
summary.affected: Payday borrowers, consumer lease customers, small loan lenders, lessors and businesses providing credit assistance are affected.
